title: Salary Sacrifice for Government Employees: Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay, including salary sacrifice for government employees. Understand tax, super, and the National Minimum Wage.
salarySummary: Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × 38 hours per week × 52 weeks, assuming a standard full-time workweek.

faqs.q: How does salary sacrifice affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice reduces your taxable income by diverting pre-tax dollars to benefits like super or cars. Government employees often use salary packaging. Our calculator does not include salary sacrifice; it assumes you receive your full hourly rate as cash. Use the ATO's guidelines for exact calculations.

faqs.q: What is the difference between casual loading and penalty rates?
faqs.a: Casual loading is a flat 25% on top of your base rate for all hours worked, compensating for leave entitlements. Penalty rates are higher pay for working unsocial hours (e.g., weekends, nights) and are set by awards. Our calculator only includes casual loading, not penalty rates.

faqs.q: How do I know if I'm paid under an award or the National Minimum Wage?
faqs.a: Most employees are covered by an award. Check your employment contract or ask your employer. You can also search the Fair Work Ombudsman's website for your industry award. If no award applies, you are entitled to the National Minimum Wage.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you're a government employee considering salary sacrifice, or simply want to understand your annual earnings, the basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time position, we assume 38 hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you your gross annual salary before tax, super, and any deductions.

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross pay would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This is the figure you'll see on your employment contract, but it's not what lands in your bank account. You need to account for tax, the Medicare levy, and superannuation.

### Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, many industries have award rates that are higher. For example, a retail employee might earn $28 per hour under their award. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details.

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of your base rate. That brings the casual minimum to $33.05 per hour. Our [the timesheet](/) calculator includes a checkbox to add this loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator will add it for you.

### Salary Sacrifice for Government Employees

Government employees often have access to salary sacrifice arrangements, also known as salary packaging. This allows you to sacrifice part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits like a car, additional super contributions, or electronic devices. The key point: salary sacrifice reduces your taxable income, which can lower your tax bill. However, it also reduces your super guarantee base and may affect other entitlements.

Our calculator does **not** account for salary sacrifice. It assumes you receive your full hourly rate as cash wages. If you are a government employee considering salary sacrifice, you should consult the Australian Taxation Office guidelines and your employer's policy. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page offers more insight.

### Fortnightly Pay and Tax Withholding

Many employers pay fortnightly. To estimate your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a 38-hour week at $30/hour, weekly gross is $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280. Your employer withholds tax from each pay based on the tax tables. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more detailed estimate.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee of 12% on your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This is on top of your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $59,280, your super contribution would be $7,113.60 (12% of $59,280). Note that super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost to your employer. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more.

### Average Earnings Comparison

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees in May 2026 were $2,083.70 per week. That's about $108,352 annually. For all employees (including part-time), the average was $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for your specific job. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page to see industry averages.

### How to Use the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) calculator is designed for simplicity. Enter your base hourly rate – the rate you are paid before any casual loading. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading. The calculator will then show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. It also estimates tax and super, but remember the limitations above.

For government employees, if you have a salary sacrifice arrangement, your actual take-home pay will differ. The calculator assumes no salary packaging. You can use the results as a starting point, then adjust for your specific situation.

### Why the 38-Hour Week?

The Fair Work Act defines a standard full-time week as 38 hours. Many awards and agreements use this as the base. If you work different hours, adjust the formula accordingly. For part-time or casual, your weekly hours may vary. The calculator assumes a consistent 38-hour week for full-time.

### Fortnightly Pay Example

Let's say you earn $35 per hour as a full-time government employee. Weekly: $35 × 38 = $1,330. Fortnightly: $2,660. Annual: $69,160. After tax (using 2026-27 rates) and Medicare, your net annual pay would be approximately $54,000 (rough estimate). Super of 12% adds $8,299.20 on top.

If you salary sacrifice $10,000 per year for a car, your taxable income drops to $59,160, reducing your tax. But your super guarantee base also reduces, so your super contributions decrease. It's a trade-off.

### Award Rates vs Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is just the floor. Most employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Children's Services Award has different rates for different classifications. Always check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. Our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page can help you find relevant rates.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual employees receive a 25% loading to compensate for lack of paid leave. This loading is applied to the base rate. So if your base rate is $26.44, the casual rate is $33.05. Our calculator adds this automatically when you check the box. Do not manually add it to your entered rate.

### Important Disclaimer

Our annual pay calculation is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. For a precise determination, consult a tax professional.

For more conversion tools, see our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page or [reference tables](/data). If you need to check your award, visit [pay guides](/blog).
